12 A uniform beam is pivoted at P as shown. Weights of 10 N and 20 N are attached to its ends.
The length of the beam is marked at 0.1 m intervals. The weight of the beam is 100 N.
At which point should a further weight of 20 N be attached to achieve equilibrium?
0.6 m
0.4 m
0.1 m
A
B
C
D
P
10 N
20 N

hints: Notice the pivot P is $0.6\text{ m}$ from the $10\text{ N}$ end and $0.4\text{ m}$ from the $20\text{ N}$ end, with $0.1\text{ m}$ marks, so take moments about P.
Remember the uniform $100\text{ N}$ beam acts at its midpoint, which is $0.5\text{ m}$ from each end and therefore $0.1\text{ m}$ to the left of P.

Compare the total anticlockwise moment from the $10\text{ N}$ weight and the beam with the clockwise moment from the $20\text{ N}$ weight, then find where an extra $20\text{ N}$ must act to supply the missing moment.
walkthrough: Take moments about P. Clockwise is taken as positive. The $10\text{ N}$ weight is $0.6\text{ m}$ left of P and the $20\text{ N}$ weight is $0.4\text{ m}$ right of P.

The uniform beam is $1.0\text{ m}$ long, so its $100\text{ N}$ weight acts at the midpoint, $0.5\text{ m}$ from the left end. Since P is $0.6\text{ m}$ from the left end, the beam weight acts $0.1\text{ m}$ to the left of P.
Anticlockwise moments about P are $10\text{ N} \times 0.6\text{ m} = 6\text{ N m}$ and $100\text{ N} \times 0.1\text{ m} = 10\text{ N m}$, giving $16\text{ N m}$ anticlockwise.
Clockwise moment about P is $20\text{ N} \times 0.4\text{ m} = 8\text{ N m}$, so there is a net $8\text{ N m}$ anticlockwise excess.
For equilibrium the extra $20\text{ N}$ must provide $8\text{ N m}$ clockwise. Required distance to the right of P is $d = 8\text{ N m} / 20\text{ N} = 0.4\text{ m}$.
A point $0.4\text{ m}$ to the right of P is the right-hand end of the beam. This is option D.

A.explanation: Point A is on the left of P, so a $20\text{ N}$ weight there would add an anticlockwise moment about P and increase the existing anticlockwise excess.

B.explanation: Point B is on the left of P close to the pivot, so a $20\text{ N}$ weight there would still add an anticlockwise moment when a clockwise moment is needed.

C.explanation: Point C is to the right of P but less than $0.4\text{ m}$ from P, so its clockwise moment $20\text{ N} \times d$ is less than the $8\text{ N m}$ needed to balance.

D.explanation: At $0.4\text{ m}$ to the right of P a $20\text{ N}$ weight gives $8\text{ N m}$ clockwise, which exactly cancels the $8\text{ N m}$ net anticlockwise moment.
